candidates.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
candidates.abstract: Large language models serve applications with diverse inference budgets, but training and maintaining separate models for each budget incurs substantial costs. Recent Looped Transformers enable flexible inference computation through parameter reuse, but maintaining strong performance across different inference budgets remains an open challenge. We introduce Accordion, a mixture-of-experts-based model that supports five inference budgets through fixed-prefix layer looping. Each budget follows a pre-defined execution path, while the minimum budget retains the unlooped model. Joint pretraining samples one budget per micro-batch and optimizes its next-token prediction loss without additional cross-budget consistency objectives. We further preserve these inference budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, where parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation integrate three domain experts into one model. After 3.6T tokens of pretraining, increasing inference depth improves Accordion-6B-A0.5B's five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of this gain using half as many additional layer executions. The final model surpasses each domain expert on its corresponding task-and-budget average, while achieving strong instruction-following performance across all budgets and retaining depth-dependent gains in mathematical reasoning and code generation.
candidates.reason: 5つの推論計算予算に対し、固定prefixのlayer looping実行経路を持つMoEモデルAccordionを提案。各micro-batchでbudgetをサンプルするjoint pretrainingとbudget別SFT/RL・複数expertのdistillationで1モデルが異なる推論深度に対応。Accordion-6B-A0.5Bは3.6T token事前学習後、追加layer実行の中間budgetで最大品質改善の89%を半分の追加layer実行数で獲得と報告。サービングthroughput実測は要旨にないが、明示的な計算予算と品質のtradeoffを提供する推論時適応計算の研究としてaccept。

candidates.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
candidates.abstract: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.
candidates.reason: multi-state linear attentionでsegmentごとのkey-query平均alignmentだけを使うroutingでは分布の広がりを捉えられない。MERLINは各segment keyの一次・二次momentを保持し、queryごとのalignment平均と分散から各stateのreadoutを重み付けする。Gated DeltaNet-1.3BとMamba-2-780MのRULER/LongBenchで改善し、4倍メモリを使うbaselineも上回ると要旨は報告。推論時の圧縮state routingで長文脈品質とメモリのtradeoffを改善する直接手法としてaccept。

candidates.title: Learning to Formulate: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Design of AI Infrastructure through Progressive Optimization and Verification
candidates.abstract: AI infrastructure, the chips and software that train and serve AI models, is designed in layers. Layers make the system manageable, but they also fix which choices an optimizer can consider. Gains that need the chip and its software to change together are excluded before optimization begins: the formulation leaves them out. Language-model agents make it possible to revisit these boundaries, but an agent's proposal cannot show by itself that a design is correct or optimal. We present Formulaic, a flow that divides the work. The agent writes the formulation, a mathematical solver optimizes within it, and verification and measurement check its assumptions and results. The agent refines the problem step by step, from the computation graph toward the chip. Each step is a template: a family of programs with the conditions under which they are correct. Wall relaxation searches the chip by pricing the hardware limits that bind the software. This paper takes a first step, through separate studies rather than one end-to-end run. On NVIDIA GB10, templates the agent wrote run complete Qwen3-8B layers $1.075\times$ faster than SGLang. In a simulated Ventus GPU study, joint design cuts the worst-scenario cycles of Qwen2.5-0.5B to 0.428 of the reference, against 0.934 for software alone. On a five-step GEMM refinement chain, reusing proofs makes checking $2.51\times$ faster.
candidates.reason: LLM agentが計算graphからchip制約まで設計の数理定式化を段階的に生成し、solverが最適化、検証・実測が仮定と結果を確認するFormulaic。NVIDIA GB10上でQwen3-8Bの完全layerをSGLang比1.075倍高速化し、Ventus GPU simulationでQwen2.5-0.5Bのworst-case cycleを基準の0.428まで削減（software-onlyは0.934）。異なる個別studyであり単一end-to-end deploymentではない。LLM inference layerとGPU設計の共同最適化を直接評価するためaccept。

candidates.title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Multi-turn conversations with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reuse input context, but long multimodal inputs increase time to first token (TTFT). Query-aware hard pruning reduces prefill tokens but permanently excludes information that later questions may require. We propose Raincheck, a framework for deferred multimodal prefill that decouples initial token selection from later information availability. An existing pruning method selects tokens for initial prefill; Raincheck preserves and progressively prefills unselected tokens in source order using unused compute capacity during decode. Unfinished prefill continues after answer return during available scheduling gaps. Attention visibility control and affine state mapping enable context updates after generation begins in full-attention and hybrid recurrent models. Prefill-decode fusion reduces repeated weight reads. We evaluate Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B with 30% initial multimodal-token retention. Across both models and four pruning methods, Raincheck recovers on average 77.7% and 60.4% of the quality lost to matched hard pruning on MultiVerse and ConvBench, respectively. On MultiVerse, the SGLang implementation reduces mean first-turn TTFT by up to 24.1% relative to full prefill, with less than 0.5% increase in mean time per output token (TPOT).
candidates.reason: MLLM複数ターンで初回prefill tokenをpruneしながら、除外tokenを破棄せずdecode中の余剰計算枠や応答後のscheduling gapで順次prefillするRaincheck。attention visibility制御とaffine state mappingで生成開始後のcontext更新を可能にし、prefill/decode fusionで重み再読を抑える。Qwen3-VL-8BとQwen3.5-9B、初期30% token保持条件で、SGLang実装はMultiVerseの初回TTFTをfull prefill比最大24.1%削減し、平均TPOT増加は0.5%未満。MLLM推論時のprefill資源配分に直接関係しaccept。
